entry.title: Docker, Windows & chasing missing disk space
entry.summary: Honestly, I love Docker. Long gone are the days of XAMPP and installing dependencies on my host machine, and it works so much better day to day than Vagrant ever did. But even though I'm a Linux fan through and through, I still use Windows in my day to day development. So Docker Desktop on my host machine, WSL 2, with Ubuntu 24 running all my instances. Honestly, it works pretty well and I've been doing it this way since I left my old city (and work computer) behind. But... WSL and Docker Desktop don't store files directly in NTFS - they live inside giant .vhdx virtual disks. What's more, when you delete stuff inside Ubuntu/Docker the space is freed inside ext4 but the .vhdx file doesn't shrink; it only ever grows. Over time, that leads to those hundreds of gigs just locked up in AppData. …
